blocks.content: My apartment has one window that faces east, which means I wake up every morning to direct sunlight in my face whether I want it or not. I do not want it. I have never once wanted it. The blinds are broken. I've known how to fix them for six months. I find this character-building.

I keep the bedroom the way I keep everything else — organized to the point where my mom came over last spring, looked around, and asked if I was okay. I told her I was fine. She moved a paintbrush three inches to the left while she was talking and I spent the rest of her visit trying not to look at it.

The paints are arranged by color family on the shelf above my desk. Warm tones left, cool tones right, neutrals in the middle. The brushes stand handle-up in three mason jars — wide, medium, detail. The canvases lean against the far wall in order of size, tallest to shortest, which is a thing that I do and which I have made my peace with.

The sketchbook on the desk is the exception. It's always open. There are pencil marks on the cover and a coffee ring from sometime last year that I never wiped off because it landed at exactly the right angle and I couldn't bring myself to destroy the composition. The pages inside are the only part of my life that looks like what it actually is.
I pulled on my running clothes. Drank half a glass of water over the sink. Did not look at the blinds.
